findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "stix-feed-summary" references sensitive artifacts (bearer). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, enrich-ioc, stix-feed-summary, check-package · Private data: search, enrich-ioc, stix-feed-summary, ai-model-price · Public sink: search · Destructive: check-package.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, enrich-ioc, stix-feed-summary, check-package · Private data: search, enrich-ioc, stix-feed-summary, ai-model-price · Public sink: search · Destructive: check-package

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "search" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.
